desks.Dividends: Apple goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter, unchanged; Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7% from $0.91, its 24th consecutive annual increase), payable Dec 10. Nvidia has not yet declared its December dividend. SPY and QQQ December distributions fall outside the window. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus EPS of $2.47 and Q3 guidance of $108.0 billion revenue at 74.0% gross margin. The implied earnings-day move is about 11.2% (about 8.9% event-isolated), against a historical average of about 5% over the last 10 reports. Apple reported Mon Nov 2 after close (EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 consensus); Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: Brent settled Fri at $98.32 and WTI at $90.83, down about 16% and 13% on the week — the steepest weekly Brent drop since Covid — as the midterm result repriced Iran-war premium lower, while Hormuz tanker attacks on Nov 5 put a floor under the fall. EIA petroleum (week ended Oct 30): crude drew 0.9 million barrels against a polled build, and distillate drew 3.6 million barrels to 99.3 million, its lowest since May 2003 and 13% below its five-year average. Natural gas storage rose 77 billion cubic feet to 3,801 billion. Next catalysts: CPI, USDA WASDE, and EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook Tue Nov 10; EIA petroleum Thu Nov 12.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for SPY or QQQ this week. Put-call parity on the 18 Nov SPX options at Tuesday's close returned 19.96, in line with the 19.90 settlement. S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Oct 28 a growth/value classification change, effective before open Mon Dec 21: growth drops 12-month price momentum; value adds free-cash-flow-to-price and an intangibles-adjusted book-to-price. It is a style-index reconstitution only — no change to S&P 500 membership, weighting, or SPX option mechanics, so no parity implication.
desks.Premium: Friday-close implied volatility at the Nov 9 expiry (CBOE delayed quotes): SPY 17.8%, QQQ 26.7%, Apple 22.8%, Microsoft 25.3%, Nvidia 49.8%, Tesla 48.9%, corroborating the morning Yahoo prints within about 0.5 points for five names. All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT — a single day drives 46-63% of each 20-day realized-variance window. Nvidia's Nov 20 expiry implied volatility of 71.8% versus 61.0% at Nov 13 prices the Nov 17 earnings event; premium into this binary event is to be avoided. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names. Microsoft shows a cross-source gap (CBOE 25.3% vs Yahoo 27.1%) that is UNVERIFIED.
desks.Quant lab: Two new candidates were added to the ledger (#233, #234), with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. #233, Gene Yu's 'How Much Evidence Does a Backtest Really Have?' (score 49, WATCH), reports per-ticker splits leaking up to 52% of test rows and only 53-99 independent outcomes per category at 3-6 month holds, but reproducibility is not established. #234, QuantJourney's point-in-time observation layer (score 43, ARCHIVE), is a maintainer announcement with no verified code or multi-instrument support. The arXiv q-fin window Nov 6-7 is genuinely empty; the newest item is still 2026-11-05.

headline: Daily research brief — Saturday, November 7

items.detail: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the next two weeks, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus EPS of $2.47 and revenue of about $108.98 billion against company guidance of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. The Nov 20 at-the-money straddle implies a move of about 11.2% (about 8.9% event-isolated), against a historical average earnings-day move of about 5% over the last 10 reports. The Nov 20 expiry implied volatility of 71.8% versus 49.8% at the 2-day expiry prices the event; premium sold into the print is premium into a binary event: avoid.
items.title: Nvidia reports Nov 17, and options price a move roughly double history

items.detail: Brent fell 16.4% on the week ($117.64 to $98.32 Fri) and WTI settled at $90.83, the steepest weekly Brent drop since Covid, as the market priced a possible US-Iran deal after Democrats won both chambers Tue Nov 3. Three more tankers were attacked in the Strait Thu Nov 5, Hormuz flows run below 60% of normal, and explosions were heard on Qeshm Island Sat Nov 7 (cause UNVERIFIED). The physical market is tighter than the price fall suggests: distillates drew 3.6 million barrels to 99.3 million, a 23-year low, with a fifth straight crude draw. Watch the Sunday-evening oil reopen.
items.title: Oil's war premium collapsed, then Hormuz escalated again after the close

items.detail: October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.1% (from 4.2%), Fri Nov 6. December hike odds rose to about 77%, up about 10 points (Invezz, citing CME FedWatch), with traders raising them to about 80% from 75%. October CPI lands Tue Nov 10 at 8:30 ET — the last CPI the FOMC sees before its Dec 8-9 meeting — alongside USDA WASDE at 12:00 ET and the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook. Rates through Thu Nov 5 (FRED): 2-year 4.46%, 10-year 4.84%, 2s10s +38bp, effective fed funds 3.88%, SOFR 3.92% — no funding stress. The front-end rally predates the jobs print, so the easing read and the hike-odds jump are sequential, not contradictory.
items.title: December Fed hike odds repriced to about 77-80% on the hot jobs print; Tue Nov 10 is the week's hinge

items.detail: The Thu Nov 5 selloff (SPY -4.51%, QQQ -6.71%, Nvidia -9.72%, Tesla -11.40%) drives 46-63% of each 20-day realized-variance window; the Wed Nov 4 rally (Apple +5.17%, Microsoft +6.47%) drives the other two. Excluding the driver day, realized volatility is SPY 13.4%, QQQ 25.0%, Apple 17.2%, Microsoft 26.0%, Nvidia 37.0%, Tesla 42.4% — every headline 20-day realized figure is inflated by that single day. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names — no free IV-history source is available. Verdicts become clean only when Nov 4-5 roll out of the window (about Dec 3-4).
